breakdown.description: The given relative velocities/angles imply different axial components, contradicting the statement that axial velocity is constant.
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve the physical contradiction. The ground truth corrects the problem by recalculating the outlet relative velocity (W2) to be consistent with the constant axial velocity derived from the inlet conditions. The generated specification, however, simply repeats all the contradictory values from the original prompt (W1=150, beta1=45, W2=100, beta2=30) while also stating that the axial velocity is constant. This preserves the original error, as an axial velocity calculated from the inlet (150*cos(45) ≈ 106.1 m/s) is different from the one calculated at the outlet (100*cos(30) ≈ 86.6 m/s).
